evidence: mail.py lines 277, 410, 458, 471, 634, 675: six bare 'except:' clauses; three swallow silently with 'pass' (attachment loops), three log then continue — suppressing SystemExit/KeyboardInterrupt along with legitimate errors

widget.py widget_script (lines 127-131): finders.find(WIDGET_PATH) can return None; widget_js_etag guards against this but widget_script passes the result directly to open() without checking, causing TypeError on missing static file

base/services/bbb.py: broad 'except Exception' in _get()/_post() returns False to callers, masking whether failure was a timeout, DNS error, XML parse error, or auth failure — callers cannot distinguish transient from permanent errors

base/services/tickets.py lines 180, 216: bare 'except: logger.exception(...)' in get_tickets_for_order continue silently, returning partial ticket list without any signal to the caller that tickets are missing
Strategy-by-directory shows views/ has 312 try_catch + 253 throws + 39 returns_null + 16 result_type — all four strategies coexist without layer-level contract
load_starred_ics_token (agenda/views/utils.py) uses precise exception list (BadSignature, KeyError, TypeError, ValueError, OSError, OverflowError) and logs at DEBUG — well-calibrated
API layer (api/views/device.py, api/views/upload.py, api/auth/permission.py) consistently raises DRF ValidationError/Http404 — clean throw-only boundary
mail_send_task retry logic (lines 484-587) is well-designed: differentiates SMTP codes, applies exponential backoff, logs to order audit trail before re-raising SendMailException
geo.py: catches only IOError from external geocoding API calls and returns graceful JSON — appropriate boundary handling

agenda/views/utils.py get_schedule_exporter_content: broad 'except Exception' on exporter.render() returns None (line 243-245), caller in ExporterView raises Http404 — functional but exporter failures are silently absorbed with no context in the 404

strengths: The DRF API layer (api/views/) consistently raises DRF exceptions (ValidationError, Http404, PermissionDenied) with no mixed strategies — a developer can predict API failure behavior reliably

mail_send_task retry logic is carefully designed: SMTP error codes are categorized, exponential backoff is applied, order audit log entries are written before re-raising, and SendMailException wraps network errors at the boundary
load_starred_ics_token uses a precisely scoped exception list and degrades gracefully to (None, None) with DEBUG-level logging — context is preserved and the caller contract is explicit
Geocoding view (geo.py) catches IOError only from external HTTP calls and returns a structured JSON failure response — appropriate for a best-effort network call
Django views consistently use Http404 and PermissionDenied as the error currency for permission and lookup failures — the pattern is reliable across the view layer
error_consistency.issue_character: The issues are concentrated in service-layer bare/broad exception handlers that either swallow errors silently (attachment loops in mail.py, ticket generation) or collapse all failure types into a boolean False (BBB service), combined with one unguarded I/O boundary in the widget serving path; they are not systemic across all layers but form a cluster in the services package.
error_consistency.score_rationale: The codebase scores above the 60-anchor (significant drag) because the API and view layers are largely consistent. However it falls short of 80 (solid but uneven) because multiple service-layer functions use bare or broad catches that discard error context and in one case actively swallow SystemExit, making failure diagnosis unpredictable. The mixed strategies in views/ (312 try_catch + 253 throws + 39 null-returns + 16 result_type) also mean a developer cannot predict how a cross-layer failure propagates. The score of 68 reflects meaningful but subsystem-localized drag that requires per-file inspection rather than trust in a consistent pattern.

issues.summary: Six bare 'except:' clauses in mail.py suppress SystemExit/KeyboardInterrupt and three silently discard attachment errors
evidence: Line 277: 'except:' around renderer.render() — logs then sets body_html=None, suppressing all exception types including SystemExit
Line 410: 'except: pass' inside attach-tickets loop — ticket attachment failure is silently discarded, email is sent without the expected attachment
Lines 458, 471: 'except: logger.exception(...); pass' for invoice and cached-file attachment — same silent discard pattern; caller receives no signal that attachments are missing
issues.suggestion: Replace all bare 'except:' with 'except Exception as e:' to at least preserve chained exceptions and exclude SystemExit/KeyboardInterrupt. For the attachment loops, add a counter and log a warning on the email or order audit log if any attachment was skipped, so operators can detect systematic failures.

issues.summary: widget_script opens a file without checking finders.find() return value, causing TypeError crash if static asset is missing
evidence: widget_js_etag (lines 28-35) guards against finders.find() returning None and returns 'missing'
widget_script (lines 127-131) calls 'with open(file_path, ...)' immediately after finders.find() with no None check — if the static file is absent, open(None) raises TypeError rather than Http404
issues.suggestion: Add 'if not file_path: raise Http404()' immediately after 'file_path = finders.find(WIDGET_PATH)' in widget_script, matching the guard pattern already used in widget_js_etag.

issues.summary: BBB service _get()/_post() catch 'except Exception' and return False, collapsing all failure types into an undifferentiated boolean
evidence: Lines 204, 229: 'except Exception: logger.exception(...); return False' — DNS error, connection timeout, SSL error, XML parse error, and BBB API error all return the same False to callers
Line 436: another broad 'except Exception' returning False in the same file
Callers cannot distinguish transient network failures (worth retrying) from permanent configuration errors (worth alerting)
issues.suggestion: Define BBBError subclasses (e.g. BBBNetworkError, BBBProtocolError) and raise the appropriate type rather than returning False. If returning a sentinel is preferred for caller simplicity, document the contract explicitly and add a separate log-level distinction (WARNING for transient, ERROR for unexpected).

issues.summary: get_tickets_for_order uses bare 'except:' to silently skip ticket generation failures, returning a partial list with no caller signal
evidence: Lines 180, 216: bare 'except: logger.exception("Failed to generate ticket.")' inside a loop — the function continues and returns whatever tickets succeeded
Callers (e.g. mail_send_task) proceed to attach the partial ticket list without knowing some tickets were missing — the recipient may receive an email missing expected attachments
issues.suggestion: Replace bare 'except:' with 'except Exception:'. Consider returning a list of (filename, content, error) tuples or raising a PartialTicketError so callers can decide whether to proceed or abort. At minimum, log the order/position identifier alongside the exception so operators can correlate failures.

root_causes: Service layer functions (mail, bbb, tickets) were written with 'never fail the caller' intent, leading to broad/bare catches that trade observability for resilience — the pattern was applied without distinguishing between safe-to-ignore failures (attachment embellishments) and failures that change the observable outcome for the user (missing tickets)

The views/ layer accumulated error strategies organically across a long codebase history (try_catch, throw, returns_null, result_type all present), creating unpredictability for cross-module call chains
